name: Cross-post every newsletter issue to Bluesky, Telegram & Discord with AI

parameters.content:
## Cross-post every newsletter issue to Bluesky, Telegram & Discord with AI

### How it works

Publish once, announce everywhere. This workflow watches your newsletter's public RSS feed and, whenever a new issue appears, has AI write a platform-native announcement for each channel — short and punchy for Bluesky's 300 characters, a little more context for Telegram and Discord — then posts them automatically.

For X and LinkedIn it stops one step short on purpose: their APIs are paid or need app review, so the workflow sends you ready-to-paste drafts in Slack instead. Posting those takes thirty seconds and costs nothing.

It reads RSS, so it is ESP-agnostic: Kit (ConvertKit) public archives, beehiiv, Substack, Ghost, Buttondown — anything with a feed.

### Setup steps

Takes ≈10 minutes.

1. Paste your newsletter archive's RSS URL into **When Newsletter Issue Published**. It ships pointing at a live example feed, so you can test-run it before changing anything.
2. Add your OpenAI-compatible API key as a *Header Auth* credential (`Authorization` → `Bearer sk-…`) on **Generate Announcements with OpenAI**. Any compatible endpoint works, including a self-hosted Ollama.
3. **Bluesky:** create an app password (Settings → Privacy & Security → App passwords) and put your handle and that app password into **Authenticate Bluesky Session** — never your real password.
4. **Telegram:** @BotFather token plus your channel's chat id in **Publish on Telegram**. **Discord:** channel → Settings → Integrations → Webhooks → paste the URL into **Publish on Discord**. **Slack:** an incoming webhook URL in **Forward Drafts to Slack Channel**.
5. **Delete the channels you don't use**, then activate. The feed is checked hourly.
6. Test with a recent issue: run once manually and check each channel got its announcement.

### Customization

The whole voice of every post lives in one node — **Create AI Prompt**. Add a channel by duplicating any posting node and adding the matching section to the prompt; **Extract AI Generated Copy** splits the AI's output per channel. If you do have X or LinkedIn API access, replace the Slack drafts node with real posting calls — the copy is already generated for them. Put a *Wait* node after **Extract AI Generated Copy** to delay announcements or respect quiet hours.

## Watch the newsletter feed

Checks your archive's RSS feed hourly and fires when a new issue appears.

## Write platform-native copy with AI

Builds one prompt from the issue, asks the AI for a per-channel announcement, then splits the answer into one item per channel.

## Post to your channels

Bluesky needs a login call first; the others post directly. X and LinkedIn arrive in Slack as drafts to paste by hand. Delete the branches you don't use.
